newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake to sell kraft products mill.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake to sell kraft products mill.

text.p: Chesapeake Corp. said Wednesday it has a preliminary agreement to sell its West Point, Va., kraft products mill, four box plants and other related assets to St. Laurent Paperboard Inc. for about $508 million.
Kraft products are raw materials used to make corrugated boxes, that is, flat linerboard, wavy paper and paper pulp.
Chesapeake said the sale is a major step forward in its long-term business strategy of focusing on its faster-growing packaging and tissue operations.
The sale price includes at least $425 million in cash and up to $75 million of St. Laurent common stock. St. Laurent would also assume about $8 million of tax-exempt debt.
Chesapeake would retain ownership of its timberlands and agreed to supply the West Point mill with a substantial portion of its virgin fiber requirements at market prices for 15 years.
St. Laurent also agreed to supply paper at market prices to Chesapeake's packaging operations for five years.

The four box plants are in Richmond, Va.; Roanoke, Va.; Baltimore, Md.; and North Tonawanda, N.Y. They employ a total of about 1,750 people. The annual manufacturing capacity of the West Point mill is about 960,000 tons of kraft pulp and paper products.

Chesapeake said it expects to record a gain on the sale. Proceeds will be used to reduce debt, expand the company's stock repurchase programme and finance growth internally and through acquisitions, it said.

The deal is expected to close in early May, subject to negotiation and execution of a definitive agreement, due diligence, approval of both companies' boards of directors, the successful completion of St. Laurent's financing initiatives, and regulatory approvals.
Chesapeake, based in Richmond, Va., is a diversified packaging and paper company whose primary businesses are packaging, tissue and kraft products.

St. Laurent, based in Montreal, makes paperboard products for sale in Canada, the United States and selected international markets. It produces high-strength, white-top linerboard, one of the principal products manufactured by Chesapeake's West Point mill.
Chesapeake's stock rose 75 cents to $28 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
